analysis.investment_thesis: IIFL Finance's FY2025 net profit collapsed 71% to INR 578 Cr from INR 1,974 Cr the prior year, following RBI's suspension of its gold loan disbursements — this is not a temporary blip but evidence of a business model dependent on regulatory goodwill it no longer holds. With a 4x debt/equity ratio and OCF negative in 4 of the last 5 years, I have no desire to own this at any P/E.
key_strengths: Diversified lending book (home loans, gold loans, MSME, microfinance) provides some segment-level risk offset
Forward P/E of 8.86x prices in significant distress, leaving some recovery optionality if regulatory restrictions are lifted
FII ownership at 27.77% suggests institutional confidence in eventual normalization
key_risks: Regulatory risk is existential: RBI's March 2024 ban on gold loan disbursals, IIFL's highest-margin product, directly caused the earnings collapse
D/E of 4.01 means any NPA cycle or funding stress amplifies losses rapidly — financial leverage is the enemy of the patient investor
Net profit nine-year CAGR of just 0.5% reveals that despite appearing to grow revenue, value creation for shareholders has been near-zero
red_flags: Net profit crashed from INR 1,974 Cr (FY2024) to INR 578 Cr (FY2025) — a 71% single-year decline signals structural fragility
OCF negative in 4 of 5 years: FY2021 (-3,587 Cr), FY2023 (-5,225 Cr), FY2024 (-8,716 Cr), FY2025 (-4,781 Cr) — a lending company that perpetually consumes cash is borrowing to lend, which ends badly
Other income turned sharply negative at -INR 584 Cr in FY2025, masking the true deterioration in core operations
Promoter holding at just 24.85% — management has limited skin in the game for a high-leverage NBFC
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I avoid businesses where the regulator can shut down the core product overnight, and IIFL Finance is a cautionary tale of exactly that risk. The gold loan segment, which carries industry-leading margins, was effectively suspended by the RBI in early 2024, and the financial damage is now visible in FY2025 numbers — profit down 71%, operating cash outflows of INR 4,781 Cr, and a debt pile of INR 51,533 Cr sitting against equity of INR 12,970 Cr. This is a leverage-dependent business model that requires continuous capital markets access to function.

ROE of 4.9% for a financial services business is an indictment — any decent banker should earn 15%+ on equity. The nine-year earnings CAGR of 0.5% means shareholders have compounded at essentially zero for nearly a decade. I would need to understand what has fundamentally changed before I'd even consider putting this on a watchlist. Until management demonstrates a clean regulatory relationship and sustained double-digit ROE, this belongs in the too-hard pile.
